Building for the Future:  Upcoming AGM

As we prepare for our upcoming Annual General Meeting (AGM), we’d like to share some of the progress we’ve made over the past year, and invite members to help shape the future of Hamilton Skating Club.

Our volunteer Board has been focused on strengthening club operations, improving the member experience and building a more transparent, collaborative and inclusive organization.

We’re proud of what we’ve accomplished and especially encouraged by the positive feedback from families who have shared that they feel heard, included and supported.

A Year in Review

Improved Member Support and Expanded Programming

One of our biggest priorities has been improving how we respond to and support our members. By establishing a dedicated Membership Relations role, we’ve been able to respond more effectively to inquiries, troubleshoot registration challenges and better understand the needs of our families.

This increased attention has helped us accommodate more registrations, identify opportunities for growth and expand our CanSkate offerings by several additional sessions each week.

Together with improved registration tracking and closer collaboration with our new CanSkate Director, these changes have strengthened both the member experience and the club’s programming. Having Chris join the director team has brought his experience across programs forward, helping to build bridges between programs, supporting skater development from start to Star. 

Stronger Financial Management and Growth

We’ve introduced expanded financial tracking, budgeting and forecasting, creating greater transparency and accountability.

This work has helped us correct historical pricing imbalances, significantly reduce fees for members in certain programs and provide greater clarity about what’s included in registration fees.

Combined with increased registrations, expanded programming and stronger financial planning, these improvements have contributed to meaningful financial growth, allowing us to reinvest more into our skaters and the club’s future.

Investing Back Into Our Skaters

Through partnership with Ancaster Rotary and our skating families, we held a community bottle drive fundraiser, which funded a skater nutrition seminar series.

We also successfully hosted the Provincial Championships for the first time, receiving excellent feedback from skating officials and generating approximately $35,000 in net proceeds after expenses. 

A portion of these proceeds has supported the new off-ice equipment, and we plan to invite members to help guide the allocation of the remaining funds through a membership survey.

Recognizing Our Volunteer Community

We hosted our first annual volunteer appreciation event this summer; thank you to each and every volunteer who supports the skating club in time and energy!

Building a Stronger Club Together

Hamilton Skating Club has benefited from the dedication of many volunteers and Board members over the years. As our leadership structure has evolved, we’ve placed greater emphasis on teamwork, shared responsibilities, transparency and collaborative decision-making.

We’ve made significant progress, but we also recognize there have been challenges along the way. We’re continuing to improve our processes, communication and coordination to provide a more consistent experience for families.

Above all, we’re committed to ensuring that every skater and every program has a place at HSC, from CanSkate through recreational, developmental and competitive skating.

Looking Ahead: AGM and Board Opportunities

We believe this is the right time to welcome new people, ideas and perspectives to help guide the next chapter of Hamilton Skating Club.

Half of our current Board is required to remain in place, according to our current Bylaws, providing continuity and experience, while departing directors and our proposed Board expansion will create opportunities for new members to join.

The proposed increase in board members is subject to the club’s governance requirements. Expanding will reflect the growth and profile of our HSC community, and allow us to share responsibilities and strengthen representation across our membership as the club continues to grow.

We’re inviting nominations for General Director positions, with particular interest in individuals who can contribute to:

Member Relations: Improving responsiveness, communication and the overall member experience. This remains a key priority.
Events Leadership: Planning and coordinating club events and activities.
Fundraising: Developing initiatives that support our skaters and programs.
Communications: Keeping families informed, connected and engaged.
Skater Opportunities & Development: Identifying and supporting opportunities that enhance skater development, growth and experiences across all programs and levels.
Program Representation: Across all HSC programs to strengthen the communication and representation for all skaters 

We welcome eligible members from all skating programs and backgrounds. Previous Board experience isn’t necessary.

Directors share a responsibility to act in the best interests of the entire club, work collaboratively, respect confidentiality and contribute to responsible governance.

AGM Details and Nominations

Date: November 18, 2026
Time: 8-9 pm
Location: HSC Boardroom 

Interested in joining the Board? Please complete the linked forms below, and submit both to Lori Cherwaty, hscsecretary@hamiltonskating.ca by November 13th, 2026

HSC BOD Nomination form .pdf

Board Expectations & Responsibility Acknowledgement .pdf

Nominations and elections will follow the club’s constitution and applicable eligibility requirements.

Our Future, Together

We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and excited about what’s ahead.

Our focus remains on building a financially strong, well-managed and inclusive club where every skater has the opportunity to thrive and every family feels valued.

We hope you’ll consider being part of HSC’s next chapter.

Thank you to our coaches, volunteers, skaters and families for everything you contribute.

Warm regards,

Hamilton Skating Club Board of Directors

OUR PROGRAMS

LEARN TO SKATE PROGRAMS

Our Learn-to-Skate programs are designed to teach fundamental skating skills to people of all ages. 

Most learn-to-skate programs are offered year-round at our rink. 

Here's what you can expect at your first CanSkate session!

Pre-CanSkate Program: Ages 4-5 

This program is the entry level for beginners who are 4-5 years of age. Children are placed into groups according to ability and taught by a Professional Coach and assisted by qualified CanSkate Program Assistants. The focus of this program is to make skating fun! Skating skills taught range from learning to stand and balance to going forwards and backwards. 

CanSkate Program: Ages 5-12 

CanSkate is Skate Canada's flagship learn-to-skate program, designed for beginners of all ages. This program is beneficial to any skater with an interest in ice sports (figure skating, hockey, ringette). Participants earn badges while they learn fundamental skating skills. Skaters are placed in groups according to ability and taught by a professional coach and assisted by qualified CanSkate program assistants. When you choose CanSkate, you will enjoy a program that focuses on fun, participation and basic skill development. Note: Skaters who wish to progress more rapidly in the CanSkate program should register for two sessions per week. 

CanSkate programs are first grouped by age, and once they step on the ice, they are grouped by skating ability. Register your skaters for the age group that you feel would suit them. Once on the ice, coaches can evaluate if they are placed in the right program. 

Teen/Adult Learn to Skate:  Ages 13+ 

A skating program for teens and adults of all ages. Skaters are taught according to ability and have lots of fun! 

JUNIOR ACADEMY

Jr Academy is a 2-day commitment focusing on the advanced skating skills for the purpose of moving to STAR/Competitive Development programs. 

Competitive Base Coaches will lead the program while monitoring and tracker skater advancements. 

The Technical Director will be part of the instructor’s team on a regular basis to monitor progress.  

STAR 1-10 PROGRAMS

Skills, Tests, Achievement, Recognition - this is what StarSkate is about! 

GroupStar

CanSkate is Skate Canada's flagship learn-to-skate program, 

The GroupStar program is the next step from the CanSkate program.

Skaters working on Stage 6 would be encouraged to skate in this program.

There will be group instruction included within this program but it is considered a transition program leading into Star 1-2

There is an optional off ice component with this program offered once per week. Figure skates are mandatory for this program.  

StarSkate offers opportunities for skaters of all ages to develop fundamental figure skating skills in the areas of ice dance, skating skills, free skate and interpretive skating.

Unique to Canada, this program teaches figure skating skills in a group and/or private lesson format in a progressive and sequential manner.

Skaters have the opportunity to take Skate Canada Tests through a nationally standardized testing system. 

Skaters who want to join our competitive program usually start with our STAR program before moving into the competitive one. 

Skaters interested in Figure Skating and moving beyond CanSkate can transition to the Group STAR or Jr. Academy program. 

Adult skaters (age 18+) of all levels can discover or rediscover the joy of skating in a welcoming environment where they can work towards on-ice goals such as competition, testing, or honing their skills and maintaining an active lifestyle.

COMPETITIVE

Competitive Skate 

The competitive program at Hamilton Skating Club is unique to most.  It is not solely based on what level an athlete skates but more on their dedication to becoming a competitive athlete.  

It is a great environment for athletes to learn important life skills such as self-confidence and awareness, determination, mental fortitude and commitment through the sport of figure skating.  

Our coaching staff is made up of a great team of dedicated professional skating coaches who have a vast knowledge ranging from early youth development to elite high performance.  

In the competitive program at HSC, athletes take the opportunity to hone their skills on the ice as well as off the ice through dance and strength and conditioning classes. 

Most importantly, a learning environment based on the pursuit of improvement is the culture created by both coaches and athletes, we all learn from each other.

About Us

Welcome to the Hamilton Skating Club!

The Hamilton Skating Club (HSC) is a not-for-profit organization, sanctioned by Skate Canada, and has been developing skaters and champions since 1938. 

Our skating and off-ice programs are designed and delivered by our highly experienced and certified professional coaching staff. 

At HSC we strive to provide quality skating opportunities to help each skater develop their passion for skating and to achieve their individual goals, dreams and successes in a friendly, safe and fun environment. 

Whether you are interested in CanSkate, StarSkate, training recreationally or at the competitive level, we welcome you to our club.

Our Mission
Committed to growing, developing and meeting the needs of all skaters, all levels, and all abilities in a positive and productive environment.

Bryce Davison, Director of Skating

Welcome to Figure Skating!

My role as a coach is to help athletes challenge themselves to understand their true potential in sport and life. The determination, dedication and desire to make small improvements daily is the measure of success.

Krystyna Lazar, Director of Learn-to-Skate

Welcome to CanSkate!

We’re thrilled to have you join Skate Canada’s flagship learn-to-skate program, designed for skaters of all ages and abilities. CanSkate is all about fun, participation, and the development of essential skating skills. Throughout the program, skaters will earn ribbons, badges, and other exciting incentives as they progress.

Whether you're new or returning, we’re excited to embark on another fun-filled and thrilling season with you!

Myself as Director, our Professional Coaches, and Program Assistants all look forward to working with you. 

Club Management & Board of Directors

Danielle Musgrave-Bond, President, Hamilton Skating Club

Welcome to the HSC family!

On behalf of the Board of Directors, I would like to thank you for choosing the Hamilton Skating Club.  For over 85 years, HSC has been teaching people of all ages how to skate. The Hamilton Skating Club is committed to delivering the best skating programs to members of the City of Hamilton and surrounding communities. Our Learn to Skate, Junior Academy, StarSkate and Competitive programs are guided by Bryce Davison, Director of Skating and Krystyna Lazar, Director of Learn to Skate along with an amazing, experienced staff of professional coaches.

The Board of Directors, staff, professional coaches and volunteers strive to provide quality skating opportunities to help each skater develop their passion for skating and to achieve their individual goals, dreams and successes in a friendly, safe and fun environment. We look forward to seeing you on the ice and around the rink!

Summer 2026 Programming & Pricing Info

For summer 2026, we are excited to bring back the consistency and quality of our day and evening program offerings of the last several years, while making a few tweaks in the fee and program structure to reflect some process changes that have rolled out through the 25-26 skating season.  

This year one of our goals as a board of directors has been to increase communication to the membership on the "why and what" behind our model. 

In that spirit, please find below a detailed summary of our summer program offerings, what they include, and what is built into our fees. 

We hope that our summer offerings are clear and well explained, but please reach out with any questions to Danielle (hscpresident@hamiltonskating.ca) and/or Michelle (hscvptreasurer@hamiltonskating.ca), and we will be happy to answer them.

Learn to Skate & Figure Skating Evening Programs

We will be offering the sessions on the schedule below (photo) for our summer evening program.

Sessions must be signed up for the full 7 weeks

Figure Skating Day Programs

We will be offering the sessions on the schedules below (photo) for our summer day programs.

Star 1-3  (4 days) & Junior Academy (3 days)  
*Club Coaching + Camp included​*  

Our day sessions are priced with the inclusion of ice fees, and off-ice fees within regular programming.
The day program may be purchased for any of the 7 weeks of programming but must be purchased for the full week(s) chosen.
The Star 1-3 & Junior Academy programs will run together on the same ice session.
These programs include supervision with our summer camp early drop off, and camp activities between sessions.  
New this summer, this session will also include group club coaching by our day coaching team for both Junior Academy and Star 1-3.
This approach helps to support and engage early star skaters interested in joining the day program, but that may not yet have a private coach, or whose base coach may not be available for daytime sessions.  
If your private coach is not available for the day session, please communicate your plans to attend the day session with your coach. If you do not have a private coach, please let us know so we can communicate this to our director of skating. 
Private lessons are also available on the session for skaters whose base coach is available. Please arrange directly with your coach.
    Weekly Pricing:
Jr Academy (3 days, Tues-Thu): $275 per week
Star 1-3 (4 days, Mon-Thu):
Weeks 1-4 & 6-7: $350 per week
Week 5: $265 (civic holiday, no skating Monday) 

Star 4-Gold  (4 days) & Competitive (4 days)  
*Private Coach Required*  

Our day sessions are priced with the inclusion of ice fees, and off-ice fees within regular programming.
This program does not include camp or club coaching within the fee.
These programs will run on a Group A and Group B schedule.
The schedules alternate start times between the 2 groups through the week. The purpose of this approach is to ensure the ice is safe with the appropriate number of skaters on each session.
Initial Session A&B assignments will be communicated to parents and skaters, at least 2 weeks prior to summer session start. The director of skating development, and day coaching team, will review registration numbers and group skaters together between these 2 sessions to optimize for training groups. The Director Skater Development will group skaters according to skating levels (Comp and Star4-Gold) as much as possible, but may move skaters between sessions  at his discretion if session maximums are exceeded, to ensure ice safety for all skaters.
If your skater is under 10, and you need supervision for early drop off or late pick-up, please contact us for pricing. Daytime camp is not available for Star 4 & up, as they are on a different schedule. 
Weekly Pricing:
  Star 4-Gold & Competitive:
Weeks 1-4 & 6-7: $190 per week
Week 5: $145 (civic holiday, no skating Monday) 

*Seasonal admin fee for summer is $30

*Please note skaters joining the day programs from other clubs must have a current Skate Canada membership to skate. Non-Club skaters will be charged an additional $10/day guest skating fee as part of their session cost.

New & Important: Ticket Ice Process Changes

In years past, we have worked with the City of Hamilton to utilize ticket ice hours for additional summer program hours between 7-9 am, offering a daily session for Star 4-Gold & Competitive skaters, built into our fees as a pass-through cost.

What Has Changed?

How ticket ice costs and purchases are managed has changed . Whereas in the past we have included and managed the ticket ice costs within our summer program registration fees, earlier this year the city introduced a self-service process for ticket ice.  Parents are now required to purchase ticket ice for their skater online through the city’s web service. HSC no longer manages this cost as a pass-through.

What Does This Mean?

The summer ticket ice programming hours for the 4-day program are still offered as they have been in summers past, and skaters in these programs are strongly encouraged to attend to gain the full benefit of our summer program offering.
The ticket ice program option provides an additional on-ice session, daily for this program, totalling 4 per week of each.
However, these costs are no longer built into our 4-day summer program fees and must be purchased separately. Costs for the regular summer programming hours have been reduced to reflect this.
Ticket ice is also offered on Friday during the times indicated on the schedule, when our HSC program is not running.

Purchasing Ticket Ice

The city now offers 3 options to purchase ticket ice. 
One option that is very economical if you use ticket ice through the year, is the annual unlimited pass, which can be subscribed and paid for monthly. The annual cost is $1,419.45+tax, and can be paid for in monthly instalments of $118.29
10-packs may be purchased for $108.77. 3 of these packs would be required to utilize the ticket ice sessions scheduled for the 4-day program for 7 weeks.
Single ticket ice pricing is $14.51
If registering for the Star 4-gold and competitive day program, please reach out to us if you need the information on how to access the City portal to purchase ticket ice.

HAMILTON SKATING CLUB – Organization Communication Chart 

PROCEDURE scope:

This Procedure implements the General Reporting Policy and is intended to ensure an appropriate chain of communication is used to bring forth general concerns and/or issues. 

This procedure applies to all individuals engaged in activities (on or off ice) with the club. An individual means a person, including registrants, volunteers, parents/guardians of skaters (including minor skaters), as well as persons engaged in activities, events/competitions, and programs with and/or hosted by the club (including coaches and staff members). 

Reporting Process 

General concerns and/or issues with regards to programming (on or off ice) and procedures will be addressed in an efficient, effective and respectful manner. The general dispute report must be made in writing by email to the club within thirty (30) days of the occurrence of the dispute. Extenuating circumstance may be considered at the sole discretion of the Board of Directors. To encourage timely and appropriate resolution, any dispute reported more than six (6) months after the interaction, incident, event or situation experienced or witnessed may not be accepted if the situation is such that an appropriate investigation is no longer feasible. 

In order to do this, members are asked to communicate their concern and/or issue in writing using the following steps:  

Committees: Budget; By-Laws; Policies and Procedures; Strategic Plan; Hiring and Discipline; Competitions; Ice Show

Send an email to the Board of Directors 

The email should contain the following information: 

1. What the concern is – clearly stated concern and what result the member would like to see come out of this process. 

2. Provide detailed and verifiable support for your complaint (email chains, policies that are not being followed, etc.) 

3. The email must be signed with the member’s name.

HAMILTON SKATING CLUB – Policy and Procedure

Purpose  

The Hamilton Skating Club is committed to safeguarding the privacy of individuals and recognizes the importance of appropriately managing and protecting the personal information provided by our stakeholders, including skaters, parents/guardians, suppliers, staff, and volunteers.  

 Policy Guidelines  

This policy outlines the principles governing the collection, use, storage, disclosure, retention, and access to personal information in compliance with applicable privacy legislation. 

1.1 Collection  

The Hamilton Skating Club collects personal information solely for legitimate operational purposes or to fulfill legal requirements. Reasonable efforts will be made to inform individuals of the purposes for which their information is being collected and how it may be used or disclosed.  

1.2 Accuracy  

The Club will take reasonable steps to ensure that all personal information collected is accurate, complete, and up to date. Individuals may review and request corrections to their personal information at any time. Upon receiving a written request, the Club will promptly update the information as appropriate.  

1.3 Storage  

Personal information will be securely stored, whether in physical or electronic format, to prevent unauthorized access, collection, use, disclosure, or disposal.  

1.4 Retention  

Personal information will be retained only for the duration required to meet operational or legal obligations. Retention timelines may vary based on applicable legislation, such as employment or financial record-keeping standards.  

1.5 Disclosure  

Personal information will not be disclosed to employees, volunteers, or third parties unless required for a legitimate business function or legal obligation, and only with the individual's knowledge and consent unless otherwise permitted or required by law.  

1.6 Access  

Individuals have the right to access their personal information held by the Hamilton Skating Club. Access will be provided upon written request and in accordance with established procedures.  

  

2. Compliance and Review  

The Club is committed to maintaining the confidentiality of personal information and complying with all applicable privacy laws. This policy will be reviewed regularly to ensure continued relevance and alignment with current legal standards and best practices.

Confidentiality Policy 

Purpose  

The purpose of this policy is to provide members of the Board of Directors and committees with clear and consistent guidelines for managing confidential information entrusted to them through their roles with the Hamilton Skating Club. 

 Scope  

This policy applies to all members of the Board of Directors and committees of the Hamilton Skating Club.  

 

Policy Statement  

All Board and committee members of the Hamilton Skating Club are expected to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information obtained through their roles. Such information must not be disclosed to any individual—including family members, friends, colleagues, or business associates—unless expressly authorized by the Hamilton Skating Club, or required by law.  

Confidential information must only be used for purposes directly related to fulfilling one’s duties within the Club. Members are expected to exercise discretion and professionalism at all times, ensuring that documents and digital materials containing confidential content are not left unsecured or visible to unauthorized individuals.  

Upon the conclusion of a board or committee member’s term, all documents, materials, or records containing confidential information must be returned to the Club.  

Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action, as outlined in the Club’s General Dispute Policy and Procedure.

pages.title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
pages.body:
Hamilton Skating Club and Skate Canada Code of Ethics  

Skate Canada Code of Ethics  

 

Purpose  

The purpose of this Code of Ethics is to outline the standards of behaviour and decision-making expected by Skate Canada. These guiding principles promote a respectful, athlete-centered environment consistent with the values and mission of the organization.  

 Scope  

This Code applies to all individuals associated with Skate Canada and its affiliated organizations, including:  

-Skaters  

-Officials  

-Coaches  

-Employees  

-Board Members  

-Volunteers  

-Alumni  

-Hall of Fame members  

It also extends to parents and guardians who are involved in or observe Skate Canada-related activities.  

Code of Conduct  

All individuals governed by this Code agree to the following:  

Professionalism & Integrity  

-Conduct myself with the highest standards of ethics and professionalism.  

-Follow and promote Skate Canada’s vision and mission in an athlete-centered approach.  

-Treat everyone with respect, dignity, and sportsmanship.  

-Prioritize the well-being of athletes above competitive success.  

Positive Behaviour & Communication  

-Use fair and constructive discipline methods.  

-Avoid any harmful behaviours, such as hitting, yelling, name-calling, insults, intimidation, or rejection.  

-Communicate respectfully in all Skate Canada interactions.  

Conflicts of Interest & Manipulation  

Disclose any conflicts of interest and avoid decisions influenced by personal gain.  

Never engage in unethical conduct aimed at manipulating competition or test outcomes.  

Respect for Professional Relationships  

-Honour coach-athlete relationships and never solicit athletes from other coaches.  

-Safe, Inclusive, and Non-Discriminatory Environment  

-Refrain from exploitative, abusive, or corrupt relationships.  

-Always act with kindness, fairness, and integrity.  

-Foster an inclusive sport that respects all individuals, regardless of race, ancestry, ethnicity, citizenship, creed, gender, sexual orientation, age, ability, family status, or any other protected ground.  

-Advocate for and uphold Safe Sport principles at all times.  

-Abide by the ISU Code of Ethics at both Skate Canada-hosted and non-hosted events.  

Legal and Ethical Obligations  

-Comply with all applicable laws at the federal, provincial, municipal, and international levels.  

-Report to Skate Canada any new criminal charges, investigations, convictions, or bail conditions.  

Zero Tolerance for Abuse or Exploitation  

-Never use power or authority to coerce others into sexual activity or unethical behaviour.  

-Refrain from all sexual conduct with children or youth, including inappropriate language, jokes, touching, or exposure to sexual content.  

-Do not engage in or condone bullying, harassment, abuse, neglect, intimidation, or discrimination of any kind.  

-Use technology and social media responsibly and never to exploit, disrespect, or harm others. 

-The use of cell phones, cameras, and other mobile devices with recording capabilities (including voice, still images, or video) is strictly prohibited in locker rooms and changing areas. Devices must be turned off while in these spaces.
-Mobile devices are not to be used on the ice during training sessions. While club coaches may use a device for video capture for training purposes, the use of personal devices is restricted in accordance with this club policy.

-Immediately report any suspicion or evidence of child abuse or exploitation to the proper authorities and to Skate Canada at safesport@skatecanada.ca.  

Substance Use & Performance Enhancing Drugs  

-Do not use, promote, or possess illegal substances or performance-enhancing drugs.  

-Compliance & Accountability  

-Adhere to all Skate Canada bylaws, policies, and procedures.  

-Stay informed about updates and amendments.  

-Do not conceal violations of this Code and report misconduct appropriately.  

-Cooperate fully with any investigations conducted by Skate Canada.  

  

Consequences  

Violations of this Code may result in disciplinary action, up to and including suspension or expulsion from Skate Canada.

Safe Sport Program Policy 

Overview  

The Hamilton Skating Club is committed to supporting Skate Canada’s enhanced National Safe Sport Program, which outlines the standards and practices required to foster a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment both on and off the ice.  

Skate Canada’s Safe Sport Program is designed to embed safety, respect, and well-being into the culture of skating across Canada. The program emphasizes proactive education, robust policy development, and clear, accessible reporting processes to prevent and manage incidents of misconduct, injury, and disputes.  

As stated by Debra Armstrong, Chief Executive Officer of Skate Canada:

pages.body:
General Dispute and Resolution Policy 

Purpose  

The Hamilton Skating Club (“the Club”) is committed to fostering a safe, professional, inclusive, and respectful environment for all individuals involved in Club activities. The purpose of this General Dispute and Resolution Policy (“the Policy”) is to promote fairness, equity, transparency, and timely response in the handling of disputes.  

This Policy establishes clear procedures for the reporting and resolution of general disputes, and emphasizes the importance of prevention, accessible communication channels, and equitable outcomes.  

General disputes may include breaches of contracts, as well as violations of the rules, regulations, and policies of the Club, Skate Ontario, or Skate Canada.  

  

Scope  

This Policy applies to all individuals participating in Club activities, on or off the ice, including but not limited to:  

-Registered skaters  

-Coaches and staff  

-Parents/guardians of skaters (including minors)  

-Volunteers and Club members  

-Participants in Club-hosted programs, competitions, and events 

The Policy governs disputes between or among any of the above individuals in accordance with the Club’s General Dispute and Resolution Procedure.  

Policy Statement  

Violations of this Policy or of any Club, Skate Ontario, or Skate Canada regulations may result in actions ranging from a formal warning to suspension or expulsion from the Club. Disciplinary measures will reflect the nature and severity of the violation and will align with the Club’s bylaws and dispute procedure.  

This Policy ensures an appropriate, impartial, and timely resolution process for reported concerns.  

Reporting a Dispute 

Disputes should be reported in writing to one or more of the following Club contacts: 

Board of Directors – president@hamiltonskating.ca

Director of Skating – bryce_davison@hotmail.com 

Learn to Skate Director – canskatedirectorhsc@gmail.com 

Operations Manager – hsc.admin@hamiltonskating.org 

Good Faith Reporting 

Individuals submitting complaints are expected to act in good faith and provide accurate, truthful information. Submissions found to be intentionally false, malicious, or misleading will be treated as serious violations and may lead to disciplinary action, including expulsion from the Club. 

Review and Investigation 

Upon receiving a complaint, the General Dispute and Resolution Committee will conduct a review to assess the validity of the issue and determine the next steps as outlined in the Procedure. 

After a full investigation, the Committee will determine whether a violation has occurred and recommend appropriate actions. These may include corrective steps or disciplinary measures. 

Sanctions, if applied, will be proportionate to the seriousness of the violation and may include reprimand, temporary suspension, or permanent expulsion from the Club. 

Final Decisions and Sanctions 

The Committee will present its findings and recommended actions to the Board of Directors for a final decision. 

In cases involving multiple or repeated violations by the same individual, stronger disciplinary measures may be applied, especially when previous corrective actions have been ignored. 

Appeal Process 

Decisions may only be appealed under specific procedural grounds, including: 

A decision was made outside of the Club’s authority 

Procedural errors occurred in violation of the Club’s bylaws or policies 

Bias influenced the decision 

Discretion was used improperly 

Appeals must follow the steps outlined in the Procedure. Appeals of Club decisions may be escalated to Skate Ontario, if applicable. 

Confidentiality 

All complaints and investigations are confidential. Until a decision is issued, no individual may disclose the existence of a complaint or any related information outside of those directly involved in the resolution process, unless legally required. 

Breaches of confidentiality will be treated as serious violations and may result in disciplinary action, including suspension or expulsion from the Club. 

Timelines 

Efforts will be made to resolve all disputes promptly. However, in certain circumstances, the Club reserves the right to modify timelines outlined in the Procedure to ensure a fair and thorough investigation. 

The Club will maintain documentation of all complaints, investigations, decisions, and any resulting actions. 

Exceptions – Allegations of Misconduct 

If a complaint involves allegations of Misconduct, it must be referred immediately to the Skate-Safe Independent Third Party: 

Website: www.skate-safe.ca 

Phone: 1-833-723-3758 

Misconduct includes, but is not limited to: 

Abuse (physical, psychological, sexual) 

Neglect or grooming 

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination 

Retaliation or interference in investigative processes 

Failure to report maltreatment or inappropriate conduct 

False or malicious reporting 

Abuse of authority 

Such cases are outside the jurisdiction of this Policy and must be handled by Skate Canada’s third-party process. 

GENERAL DISPUTE AND RESOLUTION PROCEDURE

pages.body:
General Dispute and Resolution Procedure 

Overview  

This General Dispute Reporting and Resolution Procedure (“Procedure”) supports the Hamilton Skating Club’s (“the Club”) commitment to a safe, respectful, inclusive, and professional environment. The Procedure outlines a consistent and fair process for handling general disputes as defined under the Club’s General Dispute Reporting and Resolution Policy (“Policy”).  

It ensures individuals can raise concerns without fear of retaliation, and that those concerns are reviewed, investigated, and resolved in a fair, confidential, and timely manner.  

 Scope  

This Procedure applies to all individuals involved in Club-related activities, both on and off the ice. This includes registrants, volunteers, coaches, staff, parents/guardians of skaters (including minors), and participants in events or programs hosted by the Club.  

It addresses the process for:  

-Initiating and reporting general disputes,  

-Assessing complaints,  

-Resolving disputes through investigation or alternative measures,  

-Communicating decisions and disciplinary action,  

-Managing appeals, where applicable.  

  

Reporting Process  

General disputes should be reported via email to the appropriate individual, based on the nature of the concern, as outlined in the Organizational Communication Chart:  

-Board of Directors: president@hamiltonskating.ca

-Director of Skating: bryce_davison@hotmail.com  

-Director of Learn to Skate: canskatedirectorhsc@gmail.com  

-Board of Directors: president@hamiltonskating.ca 

The complaint email must include: 

A clear description of the concern and the desired resolution. 

Supporting documentation (e.g., emails, policy references, etc.). 

Complaints should be submitted within 30 days of the incident. Complaints received beyond six (6) months of the event may not be accepted unless exceptional circumstances exist, at the discretion of the Board. 

Assessment Process 

Once a complaint is received, the General Dispute and Resolution Committee (“the Committee”) will assess its eligibility under the Policy. If accepted, the Committee will establish a fair timeline and formally acknowledge receipt within 10 business days. Other involved parties will also be notified that the dispute process has begun. 

Resolution Process 

The Committee will manage the resolution process, reviewing the submitted complaint and working with the parties toward resolution. Depending on the situation, this process may include: 

Review of documentation 

Interviews with complainants, respondents, and witnesses 

Informal resolution methods (e.g., direct communication, facilitated discussion) 

Formal methods (e.g., mediation, arbitration, or full investigation) 

If a resolution is achieved, it will be documented and shared with both parties. All investigation and resolution steps will be recorded in detail. 

Upon completion of the investigation, the Committee will submit a report to the Board of Directors outlining the findings and recommendations, including any corrective or disciplinary action. 

Knowingly submitting a false or malicious dispute will be treated as a serious violation and may result in disciplinary action. 

Decision 

The Committee’s findings and recommendations will be shared with all relevant parties. Where a policy breach has occurred, appropriate disciplinary and/or remedial action will follow. Decisions will be communicated within 30 days of the resolution (or up to 60 days from the complaint's acceptance), unless otherwise specified. 

Disciplinary Action 

Disciplinary actions may include: 

Verbal/written reprimands or warnings 

Probation or suspension of membership privileges 

Restriction or cancellation of participation 

Permanent expulsion from the Club 

Remedial actions may include apologies, training, or corrective requirements such as formal counselling or payment of levies. 

All decisions and supporting documents will be securely stored by the Club. 

Appeals 

Appeals are allowed only on procedural grounds as outlined in the Policy. The appellant must demonstrate that: 

The decision exceeded Club authority or jurisdiction; 

Procedures were not properly followed; 

The decision was biased; 

Discretion was improperly used. 

The burden of proof lies with the appellant. All confidentiality requirements must be observed during the appeal process. 

Appeals may be submitted to: 

Skate Ontario 
Email: complaints@skateontario.org 
Subject Line: Appeal of Decision from Hamilton Skating Club dated DD/MM/YYYY 

The Notice of Appeal must include: 

Intent to appeal 

Appellant’s name and address 

Details of the decision and involved parties 

Grounds for the appeal 

Supporting evidence 

Appeals must be submitted within 30 days of the Club’s decision. 

Further Appeals 

Decisions of Skate Ontario may be appealed to Skate Canada, in accordance with Skate Canada’s policies.

HAMILTON SKATING CLUB MOBILE DEVICE POLICY

Hamilton Skating Club Mobile Device Policy

Document Classification: Policy

Document control:

Implementation Date:

FEBRUARY 10, 2025

Next review by board Date:

JUNE 30, 2027

1. Purpose

To protect the privacy, safety, and well-being of all skaters and members, the Hamilton Skating Club (HSC) has established the following guidelines for the use of cell phones and mobile devices. This policy supports a safe, respectful, and professional training environment for everyone and is aligned with Safe Sport principles, ensuring all participants feel secure and respected.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all members, coaches, volunteers, and visitors while at HSC facilities, including training sessions, events, and on-site activities.

3. Policy

Change Room Privacy

- The use of cell phones, cameras, and other mobile devices with recording capabilities (voice, still images, or video) is strictly prohibited in locker rooms and changing areas.

- Devices must be turned off in these spaces.

On-Ice Usage

- Mobile devices are not to be used on the ice during training sessions.

- Club coaches may use devices for video capture for training purposes only.

-Personal devices are prohibited on the ice in accordance with this policy.  

This update aligns with HSC's commitment to maintaining a safe, respectful, and professional training environment, consistent with Safe Sport principles.

4. Violation Handling

Verbal Warning

- For a first minor violation, a verbal warning will be given by a coach or HSC Board member.

- The warning will explain the policy and expected behavior.

Written Warning

- If a second violation occurs, a written warning will be issued to the member and/or parent/guardian.

- The written warning will document the nature of the violation, date, and required corrective action.

Final Steps

- Repeated violations or serious breaches of privacy may result in:

- Suspension from training sessions

- Temporary or permanent removal from club events.

- Escalation to the HSC Board of Directors for further action

- All final actions will be documented and communicated in writing.

5. Enforcement

- Coaches and HSC Board members are responsible for monitoring compliance during sessions.

- Members are expected to report any concerns regarding mobile device misuse to a coach or HSC

Board member immediately.

- This policy is enforced in alignment with Safe Sport principles to ensure the safety and well-being

of all participants.

- HSC reserves the right to update this policy as needed to maintain a safe and respectful

environment.

6. Acknowledgment

All members, parents/guardians, and staff are expected to read and acknowledge this policy. Continued participation in HSC activities constitutes acceptance of these rules and adherence to Safe Sport standards.
